all_of: the application generates a file for the user and serves it back from a fixed directory prefix
that directory prefix is served by nginx directly rather than through the framework
any_of: the generated artifact is a server configuration that shows how the directory is served
requesting the directory itself returns an index listing rather than a 403 or 404

chain.action: register an account, read the dashboard HTML and its JavaScript, and list every endpoint it calls
chain.why: the API token and every route are inlined in the page; nothing needs to be guessed

chain.action: generate one artifact with the default values and read it, including its comments
chain.why: a generator prints the deployment's own template, so the generated file discloses how the server serves its directories

chain.action: request the serving directory itself with a trailing slash and read the index listing
chain.why: an autoindex directory exposes every file written there, including files that are not the generated artifact

chain.action: download the file in that listing that is not a generated artifact, and identify it with file rather than by extension
chain.why: the archive here was a plain tar named .tar.gz, so decompressing by extension fails and looks like a dead end

chain.action: open the database it contains and check the password column width and alphabet before assuming the framework default hasher
chain.why: a 32-character hex column in a Laravel app is MD5, which a wordlist attack breaks in seconds

chain.action: log in as the cracked privileged user and read the landing page
chain.why: the privileged view renders the flag directly; no further escalation is needed

first_confirming_probe.request: generate one artifact with the default values, follow the link to its raw file, then request that file's parent directory with a trailing slash
first_confirming_probe.expected: an index listing of the directory, containing at least one file that no user generated
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the directory returns 403 or 404, or the listing contains only files matching the generated naming pattern

blast_radius: read-only apart from one self-registered account and one generated artifact, both of which are ordinary use of the feature. Do not delete files found in the listing; other players read the same directory. Crack hashes offline, never against the live login form.

verification.evidence:
the flag was read from the body of GET / on the live target, inside a

element in the page header, while authenticated as the cracked privileged account

reuse_when: an application writes a per-user file and links to it under a fixed path prefix
a generated configuration file is itself readable by the user who generated it
an nginx-branded 404 shows a prefix is served by nginx while other paths return framework-branded errors
known_traps: this target shares its fingerprint with the 2021 alias-traversal chain and matches it at full signal coverage, yet the traversal probe falsifies: the location uses root, not alias, so nothing traverses

an nginx-branded 404 means the location matched and the file is absent; a framework-branded 404 means the prefix is not served by nginx at all, which is what decides the traversal question in one request
nginx normalises dot-dot segments before matching a location, so a multi-level traversal collapses and reaches the application instead of the static prefix
the archive was a plain tar with a .tar.gz name; identify it with file before trying to decompress it
sorting parameters supplied in the query string did not reach the query here, so the boolean oracle from the older chain does not exist on this variant
